messages:
customer-ops: Heads up — our nightly billing job failed after a Redwood call. We get a structured-json parse error from the API and our downstream CSV exporter choked. Error: "type mismatch: field 'invoice.amount' expected number but got string". This started ~2am UTC.

maria: sorry about that — can you paste the request + the model output (raw) you received? any chance the customer toggled json_strict?

customer-ops: here is the minimal repro we have (redacted):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x...' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"x-large-struct","mode":"structured","schema":"invoice","prompt":"..."}'

response (truncated):
```json
{
  "invoice": {
    "id": "inv_001234",
    "amount": "1000",
    "paid": "false",
    "status": "PAID",
    "notes": null
  }
}
```

maria: thanks — that looks like three separate type issues: quoted numeric (amount), boolean as string (paid), and enum casing (status uppercase). Which schema version are you validating against?

customer-ops: schema v2.1 (amount: number, paid: boolean nullable, status: enum ["paid","unpaid","pending"]). We run strict validation and then a billing job that expects numeric amount. The validate call failed and then a downstream pandas cast threw: ValueError: could not convert string to float: '1000' 

kevin: pinging eng-runtime. Do we have any model variants that output quoted numbers/strings by design? Also is "omit_nulls" or "nullable_bool" behavior different between model versions?

kevin: quick check — model x-large-struct sometimes returns quoted numbers when temperature spikes or for short sequences (heuristic tokenization). Structured-json strict mode will treat types strictly and reject mismatches. We haven't enforced enum lowercasing, so status casing depends on model text.

julie: this caused a billing batch to skip ~120 invoices — need ETA on mitigation. We also hit a partial double-charge because our fallback converted '"1000"' -> 1000 incorrectly for one customer.

maria: immediate mitigation options: 1) re-run with schema-less ingest then coerce types server-side (quick but risky), 2) set generation params to reduce temp and add explicit instructions to return numbers unquoted, 3) toggle non-strict validation temporarily. Which do you want us to try?

customer-ops: please try option 2 first — add explicit examples and request unquoted numeric/boolean. If that fails we'll do 1. Also can you add a flag to auto-coerce quoted numerics for this tenant?

kevin: I reproduced locally using the same prompt and model. Short-term I'll push a filter for the support team behind a feature flag: when enabled it'll coercively parse quoted numerics and booleans for structured-json outputs and lower-case enums before validation, and log warnings. Will open PR + flag this morning. Noted risk: could mask real schema regressions, so flag is tenant-scoped and off by default.

support-bot: Created ticket #SR-9876 and assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1, SLA 24h.

maria: thanks @kevin — once PR is up, can you include the exact log lines so we can reconcile later? julie — I filed a billing incident and started a manual remediation run for the affected invoices.

julie: appreciated. keep me posted on the PR/flag so we can flip it for the impacted account.

kevin: will post PR link here when ready. preliminary fix included parsing helpers: ``parse_quoted_numbers=True, coerce_booleans=['true','false','null']->types`` and an enum normalize step. Testing now.

maria: closing the loop when remediation done. Thanks everyone.
